from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES:',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA:',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
    text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (p/f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(text)
    texts.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n{text}')
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print('\\n'.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import math
q=[0.8]*20
print('Uniform high-error seam passes plausibility rule:', max(q) <= 1.5*sum(q)/len(q))
print('Sigmoid endpoints at beta=8:', [round(1/(1+math.exp(-8*(t-0.5))),6) for t in [0,1]])
for p in Path('tmp/pdfs').glob('page-*'):
    if p.suffix in {'.txt','.png'}:
        p.unlink()
p=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt')
if p.exists():
    p.unlink()
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a practical stitching problem: residual misalignment where a seam crosses scene structures. Restricting dense alignment to problematic patches offers a useful, training-free way to improve existing pipelines.

Tables 1–2 show consistent improvements across three datasets totaling 79 image pairs, four seam-cutting methods, and five alignment methods, including UDIS++. For example, adding LPAM to the REW baseline improves SEAGULL SSIM from 0.638 to 0.697.

Figures 1 and 7 provide persuasive examples of repaired structural discontinuities. Flow attenuation and constrained local seam reconnection are sensible engineering choices for integrating patch corrections.

The pipeline and pseudocode are understandable. Parameter ablations and the explicit small-patch failure discussion help characterize the method. Established components and benchmark datasets are cited, and a code URL is provided.
weaknesses: The principal concern is that the quantitative evidence does not adequately establish final-mosaic quality. All four metrics measure agreement near the selected seam, leaving distortions and patch-insertion artifacts elsewhere largely unmeasured. Table 3 exposes this mismatch: removing sigmoid attenuation improves SEAGULL SSIM to 0.768 versus 0.697 for the proposed setting, despite introducing visible boundary artifacts. Systematic evaluation of whole-mosaic artifacts, through perceptual comparisons or structural measurements, is needed to substantiate the central quality claim.

The contribution beyond existing seam-guided alignment is insufficiently established. The method combines SSIM/Otsu selection, SIFT flow, sigmoid attenuation, and graph cuts; its particular modular integration may be valuable, but the claimed new paradigm and first framework require sharper differentiation from SEAGULL [22] and dense-matching seam estimation [35]. Figure 7 provides a qualitative comparison with SEAGULL and Parallax on one example, while dataset-level quality/runtime comparisons and an ablation isolating selective patch refinement from broader dense refinement are absent.

The seam-repair trigger has a consequential blind spot. Section 3.2 declares a seam plausible when max(Q) <= 1.5 mean(Q), which also accepts uniformly high-error seams. Thus, widespread misalignment can prevent LPAM from running at all. The manuscript neither evaluates this failure mode nor studies the trigger's sensitivity, weakening the claim that seam quality is dissociated from initial alignment accuracy.

The boundary-consistency argument is stronger than the formulation supports. The one-dimensional sigmoid in Eqs. (4–5) does not enforce displacement compatibility along every rectangular patch boundary, and fixing graph-cut boundary labels ensures seam reconnection rather than geometric continuity. The acknowledged failure example is useful, but the assertion that false-positive repairs cannot worsen results remains unsupported.

Efficiency and reproducibility need stronger documentation. Section 4.4 reports roughly 6–10 seconds for LPAM alone, compared with approximately 3.5–9.6 seconds for the noniterative seam cutters, so the added cost is substantial for those hosts. Image resolutions and scaling behavior are not reported. Despite the helpful code URL, the manuscript also leaves patch padding/overlap handling, SIFT-flow settings, and the local smoothness cost insufficiently specified.
